Fact.Name: Tax-exempt interest (Form 1040 line 2a)
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 2a. 26 U.S.C. 103(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/103): "gross income does not include interest on any State or local bond." 26 U.S.C. 852(b)(5)(B) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/852): an exempt-interest dividend "shall be treated by the shareholders for all purposes of this subtitle as an item of interest excludable from gross income under section 103(a)." 26 U.S.C. 6012(d) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6012): the return shall include "the amount of interest received or accrued during the taxable year which is exempt from the tax imposed by chapter 1." Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 25, Line 2a: "In general, your tax-exempt stated interest should be shown in box 8 of Form 1099-INT ... Enter the total on line 2a." and "Also include on line 2a any exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other regulated investment company. This amount should be shown in box 12 of Form 1099-DIV." Line 2a is the sum of every 1099-INT box 8 and every 1099-DIV box 12. Cents are included in the addition and only the total is rounded (p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total."). 1099-OID tax-exempt OID is not collected. Amortized bond premium on a tax-exempt bond (1099-INT box 13) is not netted: any amount in boxes 10-13 stops the return (/flowKnockoutHasBonds). Specified private activity bond interest (1099-INT box 9) is included in box 8 and is Form 6251 line 2g (form6251 /form6251Line2g; 26 U.S.C. 57(a)(5)), not this stop. Mapped to IRS1040 f1_58[0].

Fact.Name: Interest income
Fact.Description: Taxable interest income to report on line 2b of Form 1040. Form 1099-INT box 1, plus Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 1. Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1041sk1.pdf, SHA-256 d8d7b6eacabdf145) page 2: "1. Interest income — Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b". Beneficiary's Instructions (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1041sk1.pdf, SHA-256 516ed87ce8108a13) PDF p. 2, Box 1. 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(4); 662(a); 652(a); 662(b); 652(b). When Schedule B is required, line 2b is the sum of the already-rounded Part I line 1 amounts (each 1099 and each K-1 box 1). Otherwise cents are kept until the total is rounded. Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23.

Fact.Name: Penalty on early withdrawal of savings (Schedule 1 line 18)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 62(a)(9) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/62#a_9) allows, above the line, "The deductions allowed by section 165 for losses incurred in any transaction entered into for profit, though not connected with a trade or business, to the extent that such losses include amounts forfeited to a bank, mutual savings bank, savings and loan association, building and loan association, cooperative bank or homestead association as a penalty for premature withdrawal of funds from a time savings account, certificate of deposit, or similar class of deposit." Schedule 1 (Form 1040) 2026 draft, line 18: "Penalty on early withdrawal of savings". i1040 (2025) p. 95, Line 18: "The Form 1099-INT or Form 1099-OID you received will show the amount of any penalty you were charged." The deduction is the sum of 1099-INT box 2 across all interest reports. There is no dollar threshold and no cap at the interest reported in box 1: 62(a)(9) limits the deduction only to the amount forfeited. Form 1099-OID is not an input in the app (listed under unsupported income sources), so box 3 of a 1099-OID never reaches this line.

Fact.Name: 1099-INT includes interest received as a nominee
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf (SHA-256 b92f31ece57a82ea576ac96507fe5df637dbda7489a80eb28aaab88e7c87b287) p. 1, General Instructions: "Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies." The 2026 draft https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sb--dft.pdf (SHA-256 94d34f2eae6ff134bb31b8ba9d5f52961b44e029b1dec2b39db6b62ca5a6a57b) has the same text on PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1) and p. 3. p. 1, General Instructions: "You received interest or ordinary dividends as a nominee." p. 1, Line 1, Nominees: "If you received a Form 1099-INT that includes interest you received as a nominee (that is, in your name, but the interest actually belongs to someone else), report the total on line 1. ... Below this subtotal, enter “Nominee Distribution” and show the total interest you received as a nominee. Subtract this amount from the subtotal and enter the result on line 2."

Fact.Name: 1099-INT includes accrued interest paid to the seller of a bond
Fact.Description: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf (SHA-256 b92f31ece57a82ea576ac96507fe5df637dbda7489a80eb28aaab88e7c87b287) p. 1, General Instructions: "Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies." The 2026 draft https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sb--dft.pdf (SHA-256 94d34f2eae6ff134bb31b8ba9d5f52961b44e029b1dec2b39db6b62ca5a6a57b) has the same text on PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1) and p. 3. p. 1, General Instructions: "You have accrued interest from a bond." p. 2, Line 1, Accrued interest: "When you buy bonds between interest payment dates and pay accrued interest to the seller, this interest is taxable to the seller. If you received a Form 1099 for interest as a purchaser of a bond with accrued interest, follow the rules earlier under Nominees to see how to report the accrued interest. But identify the amount to be subtracted as “Accrued Interest.”"

Fact.Name: 1099-INT box 3 includes savings bond interest already reported or accrued before the bond was received
Fact.Description: Pub. 550 (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf (SHA-256 83552968a07e63d1c81e5b4f311fc0e54728b5ff9654b5a0d2ba6292c5574317) p. 25, U.S. savings bond interest previously reported: "If you received a Form 1099-INT for U.S. savings bond interest, the form may show interest you do not have to report. ... On Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 1, report all the interest shown on your Form 1099-INT. Then follow these steps. 1. Several rows above Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 2, enter a subtotal of all interest listed on Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 1. 2. Below the subtotal, enter “U.S. Savings Bond Interest Previously Reported” and enter amounts previously reported or interest accrued before you received the bond. 3. Subtract these amounts from the subtotal and enter the result on Schedule B (Form 1040), Part I, line 2." Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf p. 1, Line 1: "Include interest from series EE, H, HH, and I U.S. savings bonds."

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-INT interest that Schedule B Part I subtracts
Fact.Description: #144: any 1099-INT with /interestReports/*/hasScheduleBSubtraction (nominee interest, accrued interest paid to a seller, or U.S. savings bond interest previously reported or accrued before the bond was received). Each is reported in full on Schedule B line 1 and subtracted below a subtotal before line 2; this tool puts the full box 1 and box 3 amounts on Form 1040 line 2b and doesn't produce the subtraction, so the return stops. Cites on the three questions.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-INT boxes 10-13
Fact.Description: More than $0 in 1099-INT boxes 10-13. Box 8 is Form 1040 line 2a and is not part of this stop. Box 9 is specified private activity bond interest (26 U.S.C. 57(a)(5), https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/57), reported on Form 6251 line 2g (form6251 /form6251Line2g), and is not part of this stop. Box 13 is bond premium on a tax-exempt bond. Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 25, Line 2a: "if you acquired a tax-exempt bond at a premium, only report the net amount of tax-exempt interest on line 2a (that is, the excess of the tax-exempt interest received during the year over the amortized bond premium for the year)." That net is not computed, so any box 13 amount stops the return. Boxes 10-12 (market discount, bond premium, and bond premium on Treasury obligations) stop with it.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-INT box 9 larger than box 8
Fact.Description: Instructions for Form 1099-INT, box 9: "Shows tax-exempt interest subject to the alternative minimum tax. This amount is included in box 8." A larger box 9 means the form was entered incorrectly. The return stops so that amount is not filed on Form 6251 line 2g. 26 U.S.C. 57(a)(5).

Fact.Name: Schedule B required because of taxable interest
Fact.Description: Whether total taxable interest is over $1,500. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." "Over" is a strict comparison, so exactly $1,500 does not require Schedule B. Compared in whole dollars, the same way as /requiresScheduleBForOrdinaryDividends (income /ordinaryDividends): Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23, Rounding Off to Whole Dollars: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." The total includes Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 1 (scheduleE /scheduleEEstateK1Interest), unrounded, so this fact does not depend on /interestIncome.

Fact.Name: Schedule B required because of ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: Whether ordinary dividends (Form 1040 line 3b; Form 1099-DIV box 1a) are over $1,500. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." Instructions for Schedule B (2025) p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements." Reads income /ordinaryDividends, the whole-dollar total of Form 1099-DIV box 1a plus Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 2a (Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 23: "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"), the same rounding as /requiresScheduleBForInterest.

Whether Schedule B (Form 1040) is required. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 1, General Instructions: "You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends." and "You had a financial interest in, or signature authority over, a financial account in a foreign country or you received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust." Schedule B (2026 draft) Part III: "You must complete this part if you (a) had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends; (b) had a foreign account; or (c) received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or a transferor to, a foreign trust." The other listed triggers (seller-financed mortgage interest, accrued interest, OID or bond premium adjustments, Form 8815 exclusion, nominee amounts) are not reported in this return.

Fact.Name: Schedule B Part III questions are answered
Fact.Description: True when Part III is answered far enough to print or to stop. A Yes on line 8, or a Yes on Form 8938 after line 7a question 1 is Yes, ends the questions. A No on line 7a still needs line 8. A Yes on line 7a needs question 2, line 7b when FinCEN Form 114 is required, a Yes that every country fits, Form 8938 No, and line 8 No. No, because the countries do not fit, ends the questions. An unanswered question is not "No". 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule B PDF pp. 3–4.

Fact.Name: Print refusal: Schedule B Part III unanswered or out of scope
Fact.Description: Refuses the printed package unless Schedule B Part III can be printed in full. A Yes on line 7a question 1 prints, with question 2 (Yes or No) and, when FinCEN Form 114 is required, line 7b countries. Not an operand of /flowIsKnockedOut: an unanswered line, including an unanswered question 2, does not knock the interview out. /flowKnockoutScheduleBPartIII is this fact and /scheduleBPartIIIAnswered, so only line 8 Yes, Form 8938 Yes, or line 7b countries that do not fit knock the return out. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule B https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sb--dft.pdf (SHA-256 94d34f2eae6ff134bb31b8ba9d5f52961b44e029b1dec2b39db6b62ca5a6a57b) PDF pp. 3–4. PDF p. 3, Line 7a—Question 1: "Check the 'Yes' box even if you aren't required to file FinCEN Form 114." PDF p. 4, Line 7a—Question 2: file FinCEN Form 114 when the aggregate value exceeds $10,000 (31 U.S.C. 5314). PDF p. 4, Line 7b: list the foreign country or countries when FinCEN Form 114 is required. PDF p. 3: "Regardless of whether you are required to file FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR), you may be required to file Form 8938" (26 U.S.C. 6038D). PDF p. 4, Line 8: Form 3520 (26 U.S.C. 6048). Form 8938 and Form 3520 are not produced, so those Yes answers refuse the print. PDF p. 4, Line 7b: "Attach a separate statement if you need more space." That statement is not produced, so No on whether the countries fit refuses the print and stops the return. Question 2 unanswered, line 7b blank when FinCEN Form 114 is required, or that fit question unanswered, also refuses the print. An unanswered line 7a or line 8 is not "No", including when interest and ordinary dividends are not over $1,500. Exactly $1,500 with every asked Part III question "No" still prints.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule B Part III foreign account or trust
Fact.Description: True only when Schedule B line 8 is Yes, Form 8938 is required after line 7a question 1 is Yes, or the countries do not fit on line 7b. Wired into /flowIsKnockedOut. A Yes on line 7a question 1 or question 2 does not knock the interview out: those answers print. An unanswered Part III, including an unanswered question 2, is complete false here. The print still fails closed through /flowPrintRefuseScheduleBPartIII. 2026 draft Instructions PDF pp. 3–4 (FinCEN Form 114, 31 U.S.C. 5314; Form 8938, 26 U.S.C. 6038D; Form 3520, 26 U.S.C. 6048). Complete false when the supported Part III answers are in place, including exactly $1,500 with every asked question No (2026 draft Instructions PDF p. 2: "over $1,500").

Fact.Name: Schedule B Part I line 1 payer 1
Fact.Description: Schedule B (Form 1040) Part I line 1. Form 1099-INT rows are listed first, then each estate or trust with Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 1 greater than zero. Beneficiary's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) (2025) (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1041sk1.pdf, SHA-256 516ed87ce8108a13) PDF p. 2, Box 1: interest is reported on Schedule B Part I line 1 if applicable. The K-1 payer is the estate or trust name. The amount is the whole-dollar taxable interest or rounded box 1. 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(4); 662(b); 652(b). A row past the 14 printed lines is in the line 2 total and is not printed.

Fact.Name: Schedule B Part II line 5 payer 1

The amount is the whole-dollar ordinary dividends or rounded box 2a. Line 6 is income /ordinaryDividends, the rounded total, which can differ by $1 from the sum of these rows when there are cents. 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(7); 662(b); 652(b).
